$description: Porchlight design tokens for SeniorSocial. W3C Design Tokens Community Group draft format. Token values define colour, typography, spacing, motion and target size. Contrast calculations use the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula.

palette.$description: Raw ramps. Never referenced by a component. Components reference color.semantic.* only.

50.$description: Easy Mode alternate surface. Warm near-white.

100.$description: Standard Mode page ground. The porch light on a painted wall.

200.$description: Standard Mode recessed surface: chips, table stripes, the print band.

300.$description: Hairline rules only. 1.296:1 on linen.100 — decorative, never the sole boundary of a control.

400.$description: Subtle border and disabled glyph. 3.356:1 on linen.100. BANNED as text at any size in this product.

700.$description: Control border. 3.860:1 on linen.100, 4.158:1 on white. Out of luminance order on purpose: named for its role, not its darkness.

800.$description: Standard Mode body ink. 13.494:1 on linen.100.

900.$description: Easy Mode body ink. 17.740:1 on white.

600.$description: Hover fill for the Standard primary button. 5.031:1 on white.

700.$description: Standard Mode primary. White on it = 6.932:1.

800.$description: Easy Mode primary. White on it = 9.087:1.

900.$description: Pressed state and high-contrast primary. White on it = 11.861:1.

700.$description: Porch Amber. Standard Mode accent. 4.661:1 on linen.100 — passes AA text, fails the 7:1 Easy Mode bar.

500.$description: Focus lantern. 1.621:1 on linen.100 — CANNOT carry the focus indicator alone. Used only as the inner band of the two-band ring, where it reads against dark fills (3.970:1 on harbor.700, 5.204:1 on harbor.800, 4.049:1 on brick.700, 8.325:1 on ink.800).

semantic.$description: Three themes. standard and easy are both shipped in the MVP; highContrast is the forced-colors / user-selected maximum-contrast theme required by RFP A-2.

disabled.$description: Contrast-exempt under WCAG 1.4.3. Never the only signal that a control is unavailable: pair with the word 'not available' and a reason.

hairline.$description: 1.296:1. Decorative rules only. A build lint fails if this token appears on an input, checkbox, radio, select, or clickable card.

control.$description: 3.860:1 on canvas. Every control whose boundary is the affordance.

easy.$description: Same hues, higher floor. Every foreground/background pair in this theme meets or exceeds 7:1, which is why the canvas is white rather than Linen: amber.800 on linen.100 is 6.975:1, 0.025 short of the bar, and on white it is 7.514:1.

muted.$description: Easy Mode has no third text weight. muted is an alias of secondary so that no Easy Mode text drops below 7.851:1 on white.

hairline.$description: Easy Mode has no hairline. The token resolves to the control border so that a decorative rule authored for Standard Mode does not vanish for a low-vision user.

highContrast.$description: Selected by the person, or forced by the OS. Under forced-colors the browser overrides most of this; the theme exists so that the person can reach maximum contrast without leaving the product, and so that the forced-colors fallback is authored rather than accidental.

sans.$description: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, self-hosted WOFF2 subset (Latin + Latin-1 Supplement, which covers the Spanish diacritics and the inverted marks). Open licence. Chosen for disambiguated letterforms: the Braille Institute drew it so that b/d, i/l/1, 0/O, and rn/m do not collapse at low acuity. Fallback chain is deliberate: every fallback is metric-tolerable, and the stack never falls to a serif.

mono.$description: Confirmation codes, ride ids, case numbers, and the CSV import preview only. Never body text.

weight.$description: No weight below 400 exists in this product. Italic is available in the family but is forbidden for any run longer than three words.

xs.$description: 14px. Timestamps and legal footnotes only. Never a sentence a decision depends on.

base.$description: 18px. Body. Above the 16px absolute floor from the senior-UX guidance in the cycle-1 research digest section 8.

lg.$description: 20px. Primary line of a list item; the answer text in the concierge.

4xl.$description: 44px. The single number on a status screen; the pickup time.

sm.$description: 18px. The smallest type that exists in Easy Mode. Timestamps and the 'as of' line.

lg.$description: 26px. The label on the single action.

xl.$description: 32px. The question the screen is asking. Easy Mode has exactly one heading level.

2xl.$description: 40px. A time, a date, or a confirmation code shown alone.

wide.$description: WCAG 1.4.12 requires text to survive 0.12em letter-spacing. Used natively only on the confirmation-code display.

standard.$description: Maximum line length for body copy.

easy.$description: Narrower on purpose: at 22px a 70ch line is a return-sweep failure for a reader with central-vision loss.

spacing.$description: 8-point grid with a 2px and 4px sub-step for optical alignment only. Easy Mode does not invent new values: it steps up one or two rungs (12 becomes 20, 16 becomes 24, 24 becomes 32).

targetGap.$description: 12px. Minimum clear space between two adjacent activatable targets. Satisfies WCAG 2.2 2.5.8's spacing exception with room to spare and is the single most useful token for a tremor.

focusOffset.$description: Gap between the control edge and the inner focus band, so the ring is never mistaken for part of the control.

shadow.$description: Shadow is a Standard Mode affordance only. In Easy Mode every shadow token resolves to none and elevation is expressed as a 3px border, because a 4px blur at 10% opacity is invisible at 300% zoom and to a screen reader alike.

fast.$description: Colour and opacity changes on hover and focus.

base.$description: The ceiling for anything a person has to wait through. Spine section 7: motion never exceeds 200ms.

slow.$description: Reserved for a full-screen route transition in Standard Mode. Not used in the MVP.

reducedMotion.$description: Flag, not a duration. When 1 — set by prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, by the person's own toggle, or unconditionally in Easy Mode — every transform, translate, scale and parallax is removed, every duration resolves to motion.duration.instant except colour and opacity which resolve to motion.duration.fast, and every auto-advancing surface (carousel, marquee, auto-dismissing toast, auto-refreshing queue) stops and gains a manual control. This is the only token that is allowed to change behaviour rather than appearance, and the a11y test layer asserts it.

autoAdvance.$description: Always 0 in this product, in both modes. There is no auto-advancing content anywhere: no carousel, no auto-dismissing toast, no timed redirect. Present as a token so that a builder who wants one has to change a token and face the ui-agent.

min.$description: 44px. Standard Mode floor. WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 asks 24px; the platform guidelines ask 44px; we take 44px.

easy.$description: 48px. Easy Mode floor, from the senior-targeted 48x48dp recommendation in the cycle-1 research digest section 8.

priority.$description: 56px. The Priority Assistance button and the Easy Mode bottom-bar buttons.

inline.$description: 20px. Inside a line of Standard body text.

control.$description: 24px. In a Standard button, beside its text label.

easy.$description: 32px. In an Easy Mode button, beside its text label.
88px. Height of the persistent Easy Mode bottom bar, reserved as body padding so it never covers content or a focused control (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11).

headerMax.$description: A sticky header may never exceed this. Above it a focused control at the top of the viewport can be fully obscured, which is exactly what 2.4.11 forbids.

crisisBanner.$description: Highest layer in the product on purpose. The 911 and crisis line may never be covered by a dialog, a toast, a cookie notice or a chat launcher.

reflowFloor.$description: 320px. WCAG 1.4.10: every screen must work at 320 CSS px wide with no two-dimensional scrolling. Equivalent to a 1280px viewport at 400% zoom, which is how Galina (AR-10) reads.

easyMaxColumns.$description: Not a length. Easy Mode is one column at every breakpoint, including a 27-inch desk monitor at the senior centre.

porchlight.themeStatement: A light left on for you. Warm, calm, legible, dignified: the product looks like a neighbour's porch at dusk, not a government form and not a hospital.
porchlight.formula: WCAG 2.x relative luminance. For each channel c of 0-255: cs = c/255; cl = cs/12.92 if cs <= 0.03928 else ((cs+0.055)/1.055)^2.4. L = 0.2126*Rl + 0.7152*Gl + 0.0722*Bl. Contrast = (Llighter + 0.05) / (Ldarker + 0.05). All ratios below were computed with this formula and are reproduced to three decimals; the worked arithmetic for the load-bearing pairs is in 06-ui-ux-system.md section 2.

bars.note: Standard Mode is held to WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text). Easy Mode is held to 7:1 for every text pair, which is AAA, because Easy Mode exists for the people for whom AA is not enough.

changesFromSpine.spineValue: Lantern #FFB703 3px ring with a 2px ink offset
changesFromSpine.newValue: two-band ring: outer 3px ink (#1F2A37 Standard, #111827 Easy), inner 2px Lantern #FFB703, 2px offset from the control edge
changesFromSpine.reason: Lantern against the Linen ground computes to 1.621:1, which fails WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for a non-text indicator. No amber that still reads as amber reaches 3:1 on a near-white ground — #C98A00 only reaches 2.738:1 and #E5A302 only 2.037:1. Reversing the band order puts ink (13.494:1 on Linen) against the page while keeping Lantern where it earns its place: against dark fills, where ink is only 2.097:1.

changesFromSpine.newValue: #8A3F07 in Easy Mode; #B4530A retained in Standard Mode
changesFromSpine.reason: #B4530A is 4.661:1 on Linen — AA, but short of the 7:1 floor the spine itself sets for Easy Mode. #8A3F07 is 7.514:1 on white.

changesFromSpine.newValue: #24552E in Easy Mode; #2E6B3A retained in Standard Mode
changesFromSpine.reason: #2E6B3A is 5.943:1 on Linen, short of 7:1. #24552E is 8.700:1 on white.

changesFromSpine.newValue: #7F2323 in Easy Mode; #A32D2D retained in Standard Mode
changesFromSpine.reason: #A32D2D is 6.562:1 on Linen, short of 7:1. #7F2323 is 9.690:1 on white.

changesFromSpine.spineValue: not stated; Linen #FAF6EF implied by 'the same hues'
changesFromSpine.reason: amber.800 on Linen is 6.975:1, 0.025 short of the 7:1 floor. Rather than push the accent darker until it stops looking like a porch light, the Easy canvas moves to white, where every Easy pair clears 7:1 with margin. The warm ground stays in Standard Mode, which is where most people will see it.

The spine had no border colour. The obvious neutral #7A8899 computes to 3.356:1 on Linen and 3.022:1 on the Linen-200 chip ground — inside 3:1 but one rounding from failing. #6E7E90 gives 3.860:1 and 4.158:1 and leaves headroom. #7A8899 survives as border.subtle for decoration only.

changesFromSpine.newValue: #E4D9C6 (color.palette.linen.300), decorative only, forbidden on controls by lint
changesFromSpine.reason: 1.296:1. Legitimate as a table rule where the rule carries no information, illegal as the boundary of an input. Recorded here so nobody discovers the difference by shipping it.

bannedTokens: color.palette.* referenced directly by a component
color.palette.ink.400 used as text at any size
color.palette.linen.300 used as the boundary of a control
any hex literal in a component file
any px literal for a font size, target size, or spacing value
colour as the only carrier of a status, an error, or a required field
